solves.reason: Newspaper revenue dropped (not risen); graph displays (not conceals) data; most popular activity (not rare) = sending emails. dropped-displays-popular matches option 1.

Revenue 'had continuously dropped' (steady trend fits continuously not occasionally); North America 'closely followed by' Europe; most popular activity 'completed' online (not abandoned). continuously-closely-completed = option 2.

Internet revenue increased and in 2013 surpassed (not trailed) TV; graph displays (not conceals) expenditures; most popular activity completed (not abandoned) online. surpassed-displays-completed = option 3.
Text states Asia Pacific CONSUMED the largest percentage of oil, not produced (Middle East produced the most). Sentence ④ incorrectly uses 'produced' for Asia Pacific, contradicting the passage.
Newspaper ad revenue 'continuously climbed' contradicts the passage which says it continuously dropped/declined since 2005.
'Internet ad revenue had noticeably dropped' is wrong — passage says it increased (surpassed broadcast TV in 2013), not dropped.
'total consumer __________ for camping fees and camping equipment' matches 'expenditures' (spending), consistent with 'spent the largest amount of money' in next sentences.
'smallest percentage point __________ between oil production and consumption' = gap, matching the production-vs-consumption comparison theme.
'second most __________ Internet activity in 2016' = common, paralleling 'most popular/common activity' phrasing used elsewhere in the passage.
'higher' (percentage was higher than girls' by 4 points) is closest in meaning to 'greater'.
'proportion' (of certificates) means 'share' — a portion/percentage of a whole.
'completed' (activity completed online) is closest to 'finished'.
'lower' (percentage points lower) is opposite of 'higher'.
'consumed' (oil consumed) is opposite of 'produced', matching the production vs consumption contrast in the passage.
(A) 'spent the afternoon reading' = spent time → '시간을 보내다'. (B) 'spent money on camping fees' = spent money → '돈을 쓰다'. Matches option 1.
Definition 'income a company/organization receives regularly, especially from selling goods/services' = 'revenue'.
The blank modifies the verb 'increased' (adverb needed): 'increased steadily since 2005', matching the base word 'steady' in adverb form.
Passive past participle modifying the activity: 'finding information..., undertaken by more than 70% of adults' — matches original passage wording.
Passage states radio revenue 'changed little, remaining around 15 billion dollars' between 2009-2013, unlike other media types — matches 'changed little'.
Passage states 'Hairstylists and barbers had the smallest proportion in the category of high school or less' — direct match.
